question: Is the page 1 photo the agency's own? A second reviewer found: p1 photo (soldier in OCP holding two children's hands by a house porch, sketch-filtered) is uncredited and posed; it was also uncredited in the 2018 predecessor and no DVIDS/agency source was found. Ruling 1 would take it as the agency's own unless evidently from elsewhere; it looks commissioned/stock-like, same doubt as the OSHA 3080 precedent. Text and release fine. Yes lists it under ruling 1; no keeps it out.

question: Does "reviewed and incorporated" count as a credit to an outside work? A second reviewer found: p2: 'The following references were reviewed and incorporated into this fact sheet' - ISID 2022, Morgan 2004, PAHO 2004, PAHO/ICRC 2016. Under ruling 2 'incorporates a named outside work' counts as a credit on what it covers; the text reads as DHA's own summary and no wording looks lifted, but 'incorporated' is the trigger word. No pictures of concern.

Berte, USA, retired, formerly of the AFPMB), the 2024 reviser (Joshua Bast, DCPH-A) and reviewers from USDA and the Army, all federal; Appendix C (pages 18-20) summarises louse-control recommendations of WHO, PAHO and APHA with citations and quotes one sentence from a 1997 WHO fact sheet in quotation marks: citations under ruling 2, nothing credited as adapted or reprinted; 'NATO' and 'University' appear only in a personal-communication note and the reference list. Picture audit: the only picture page is the cover (page 1), looked at by eye: the DoD seal and the DOPSR clearance stamp; no other images or drawings. Note: page 2 repeats the title of another guide ('Guidelines for Testing Experimental Pesticides on DoD Property'), a typing slip. Scope flag for the owner: the method (wash clothing at 54 C/130 F for 15 minutes or hotter, tumble-dry at 60 C/140 F, field hot-water baths, bathing; body lice live in clothing) is general-use disaster and camp sanitation and matches current CDC advice, but the guide is framed for detainee and displaced-civilian camps under DoD control: pages 5-8 and Appendix B are DoD doctrine and responsibilities, and Appendix D lists DoD-supply permethrin uniform kits.
question: Is it in scope? A second reviewer found: Scope: written for detainee/dislocated-civilian camp operations under DoD control - Appendix B is JP 3-07/JP 4-02/DoDI 2310.08 doctrine, the method centres on the LADS laundry system, Appendix D lists DoD-supply NSNs; Appendix C summarises WHO/PAHO/APHA and quotes one WHO sentence. Only about one page (54 C wash, 60 C dry, bag clothing) is general-use. Release and pictures fine.

title: Aerographer's Mate Module 5: Basic Meteorology
licenceNote: US government work (17 U.S.C. 105). NAVEDTRA 14312, June 2001, cover and title page: Distribution Statement A, approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. Preface: "2001 Edition Prepared by AGC(AW/SW) RICK KROLAK", a Navy chief, "Published by Naval Education and Training Professional Development and Technology Center". The file is a Wayback Machine raw capture (15 December 2001) of the Navy's official NETPDTC address advancement.cnet.navy.mil/products/web-pdf/tramans/fullbook/14312.pdf. This answers the earlier rejection in REJECTED.md, which rested only on the militarynewbie.com copy having no second copy. SHA-256 4db1051d3b274b80decf85ec12c9415e0683b5888a996dce98078e4b5f6e0954.
evidence: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. (cover, PDF page 1; repeated on PDF page 2)
creditsNote: Whole text searched and every hit read in context. Hits: the course answer-sheet boilerplate, "taken from" in physics text, two Air Weather Service (US Air Force) publications, AWS/TR-79/006 and AWS/TI-84/001, and "your local power company" in a question. Picture audit, 20 November 2026: every page with a picture (90 of 252 pages) was looked at by eye, with zooms on anything small. No picture carries a credit line, copyright notice, signature, watermark, logo or brand. Open point for the owner: Figure 6-2 (PDF page 168), a Navy redraw with figure id AG5f 0602, is titled "CLIMATIC TYPES OF THE EARTH (after Köppen)". "After" says the map is adapted from Wladimir Köppen (died 1940). His classification and maps appeared between 1900 and 1936, so whether the source is long out of copyright (the Beaufort case in ruling 2) depends on which map was followed. No other source is printed on the map (zoomed). Table 6-2, "Trewartha's Climatic Groups and their Poleward Boundaries", states a named classification's boundaries in the Navy's own typeset table with no credit line, so it is taken as a summary (a citation). Uncredited photographs: solar-disk photographs (Figure 1-2, page 14), a four-frame tornado sequence (Figure 5-6, page 147) and scanned world pressure maps (Figures 3-3A/B, page 60). Each carries a Navy figure id and no marks when zoomed, and none is stock imagery or a product photograph, so they are taken as the Navy's own. Figure 1-10 (page 29) has a small engraving-style wind-head drawing with no signature (zoomed to 500 dpi). Page 97 carries the standard US government note that international boundaries are not necessarily authoritative. Text: the 7 pages without a text layer are all blank; scrambled lines 0.02 percent (PyMuPDF) and 0.1 percent (pdftotext). No safety advice beyond mentions; page 5-11 repeats the dated idea that pressure drop makes buildings explode in a tornado, without advice.
question: Is Figure 6-2 (PDF page 168), a Navy redraw titled "CLIMATIC TYPES OF THE EARTH (after Köppen)", the Navy's own? "After" says it is adapted from Wladimir Köppen's classification (he died in 1940); no credit line or other owner is shown. Everything else is clean (see creditsNote). Yes lists it; no keeps it out.
